key_insight: ShapeCond leverages time-series-specific shapelets (local discriminative motifs) to guide synthesis of a tiny, high-fidelity training set, enabling fast dataset condensation that preserves temporal structure image-centric methods miss.
problem_solved: Existing dataset condensation approaches are designed for images and often fail on time series because they ignore local temporal motifs; ShapeCond addresses the challenge of creating compact, informative synthetic time-series datasets that retain class-discriminative temporal patterns.
method: Extract class-discriminative shapelets (local motifs) from the original time-series data to capture temporal signatures.
Optimize a small set of synthetic time-series so their shapelet activations (or shapelet-guided gradients) match those of the full dataset, ensuring preserved discriminative structure.
Use shapelet-aware initialization and lightweight optimization to make condensation fast and scalable for time-series classification tasks.
impact: Allows ML practitioners to train and iterate time-series classifiers much faster using far smaller synthesized datasets while preserving classification-relevant temporal motifs—reducing storage, compute, and deployment costs.
visual_elements: Shapelet extraction diagram: raw time series with highlighted local motifs and extracted shapelets per class.
Before/After condensation chart: dataset size vs. classification accuracy (or performance retained) illustrating compression with minimal loss.
Condensed-sample schematic: a few synthetic series annotated to show embedded shapelets that drive class decisions.
Performance summary bar chart: training time and memory savings (speedup) compared to full-data training and image-centric condensation baselines.
paper_title: ShapeCond: Fast Shapelet-Guided Dataset Condensation for Time Series Classification
paper_authors: Sijia Peng, Yun Xiong, Xi Chen, Yi Xie, Guanzhi Li
